analyzed_vuln.description: In concat_function(), when `result == op1` and `free_op1_string` is true, the code calls `i_zval_ptr_dtor(result)` (line ~2062) before extending/reusing `op1_string`. In this PoV, `result/op1` can hold an exception object zval (from failed DateTime construction). Destroying `result` drops the last ref and frees the object, but the same freed zval remains reachable in EG(symbol_table). During request shutdown, `shutdown_destructors()` iterates the symbol table and `zval_call_destructor()` reads refcount from that dangling object, causing heap-use-after-free. Root cause is unsafe in-place concat destruction order/alias handling in concat_function, which can free a still-referenced symbol-table zval.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires an in-place concatenation path (`.=`) where VM passes `result == op1`, and conversion/exception paths set `free_op1_string` so concat_function executes the `i_zval_ptr_dtor(result)` branch. The PoV repeatedly performs `.=` operations and invokes `new DateTime(...)` with malformed input to create/catch exceptions, producing an object value that is prematurely destroyed during concat. The stale object zval persists in the symbol table until `php_request_shutdown -> shutdown_destructors -> zend_hash_reverse_apply(zval_call_destructor)`, where refcount access on freed memory triggers ASan UAF.
